absent: Numeric expansion of the shared register, instruction, bit and mask constructors and final thirty-two-bit encodings.
Architectural side effects, required barriers, ordering and trapping behavior of the translate, TLB, branch record, guarded stack and resync operations.
Values of reserved-one masks, EL1-specific control bits, granule shift and fifty-two-bit and physical-range symbols, and sanitizer tag bounds referenced but not defined here.
Conditions selecting among the alternative endianness, range, granule and exclusion definitions.
Lock rules, calling contexts, state machines, entry points and data structure layouts; none appear in these fragments.

findings.text: EL2 interrupt virtualization controls are exposed as a small family covering virtual error injection, system register enable, maintenance interrupt status and empty list status. They share common leading encoding fields and differ only in trailing selectors, denoting a contiguous guest interrupt control block.

Sixteen virtual list registers are organized as two banks of eight. The first bank and second bank are distinguished by different middle selectors while the per-register index selects the final field, so a bank helper plus index zero to seven names each register.

EL2 provides context identity, thread identity and software context number registers, parameterized activity monitor virtual offset controls for two groups with index bits split across middle and final fields, and hypervisor timer state comprising offset, control and physical plus virtual timer value and compare triplets.

EL1 state aliases accessible from EL2 for nested virtualization cover translation bases, saved status and return address, fault address and status, tag fault status, profiling control, memory attributes, vector base, context number, counter access and physical plus virtual timer triplets, alongside a branch record control and the EL2 stack pointer. The aliases share a distinct second encoding field from native EL1.

Address translate operations use a fixed leading code and control field, with EL1 versus EL2 accessibility distinguished by the second field. Variants cover stage one EL1 and EL0 reads and writes, permission-checked reads, access flag update, EL2 stage one operations and combined stage one plus two translations for EL1 and EL0.

TLB maintenance encodings share a fixed leading code with separate selectors for minimum exception level, pacing distinguishing the common extra-slow form from the rarely used non-extra-slow form, and shareability plus range class distinguishing inner, outer and non-shareable, range versus single, and stage two inner versus outer and non-shareable cases.

EL1-accessible maintenance forms a product of operation shape, shareability and pacing. Shapes include full VM invalidate, VA by address, ASID-scoped, address with ASID, last-level and last-level with ASID, each with range counterparts. Each shape appears in outer-shareable, inner-shareable and non-shareable forms and is duplicated in extra-slow and non-extra-slow pacing.

EL2-accessible maintenance adds full EL2 invalidate, VA at EL2, full EL1 invalidate, last-level at EL2, combined stage one plus two VM invalidate, and stage two IPA by address with range, last-entry and range-last-entry counterparts. As with EL1, each appears across shareability classes and in both extra-slow and non-extra-slow pacing.

Miscellaneous system instructions comprise guarded control stack push and pop variants including a mode-switching push, branch record invalidate-all and inject, and four context resync operations for control flow prediction, data value prediction, common operation and private permission state.

The two branch record maintenance operations are also available as pre-encoded instruction words that combine a system instruction base pattern with the operation encoding and a fixed field denoting no architectural register destination.

Generic system control bits occupy fixed positions from high to low: trapping of preserve-aspect state, speculation barrier behavior, allocation tagging, fault barrier, pointer authentication enables and load-store alignment behavior, endianness and error handling controls, context extension trapping, execute-never, branch authentication, cache, exit semantics and low alignment plus cache plus MMU enables, with dedicated shift constants for the endianness and one authentication enable.

The EL2 control word has MMU-on and MMU-off compositions. MMU-on combines MMU, cache, alignment, instruction cache, implicit error synchronization, execute-never, endianness selection, fault barrier, error isolation and exit semantics plus a reserved-one mask. MMU-off contains only reserved-one plus endianness selection. Endianness selection has two build variants selecting either the endianness bit or zero.

The EL1 control word has MMU-off and MMU-on compositions. MMU-off combines endianness selection with alignment, tagging, error isolation, context trapping and exit semantics. MMU-on adds MMU, cache, stack alignment checks, debug and trap controls and pan and speculation controls to the same base. Endianness selection has two build variants selecting either combined endianness bits or zero.

Memory attribute byte values distinguish device non-gathering non-reordering non-early-ack, device non-gathering non-reordering early-ack, normal non-cacheable, normal tagged and normal cacheable, with a full-byte mask. An index helper places an attribute into an indexed eight-bit slot by shifting by eight times the index.

Memory model feature bounds define supported ranges per translation granule and physical address size. Four kilobyte and sixty-four kilobyte minima are zero with maxima seven, sixteen kilobyte minimum is one with maximum fifteen, each large-page-extension alias maps to its fifty-two-bit variant, minimum physical range is thirty-two bits, and the second granule field distinguishes default, none, minimum and large-page-extension values up to seven.

Maximum physical range and generic granule selectors are build-time aliases. The maximum selects either the fifty-two-bit or forty-eight-bit variant. The generic granule shift, large-page-extension value, supported minimum and maximum and second-shift identifiers select the four kilobyte, sixteen kilobyte or sixty-four kilobyte specific variants respectively, so exactly one page-size family applies per build.

Floating point, matrix extension and vector extension trap controls each use an adjacent bit pair distinguishing EL1 access enable from EL0 access enable conditional on EL1 enable, located in distinct bit pairs in the upper half of the low control halfword.

Memory tagging controls comprise a random-tag bit and sixteen-bit exclusion mask, an include mask derived from the low nibbles of the sanitizer tag minimum and maximum and inverted against the exclusion mask, a kernel default combining random generation with the exclusion, a low-nibble tag mask plus sixteen-bit seed at mid-byte shift, and per-regime fault bits at the two lowest positions. The kernel exclusion has two build variants: sanitizer-derived or full mask.
A safe identifier value is defined with only the top bit set, providing a valid but non-matching multiprocessor affinity where no real processor identity must be reported.

Register and instruction identifiers are built from five numeric fields through shared constructors, with tiny index helpers deriving middle and final fields for list-register banks and activity monitor offsets. This yields compact indexed families in which neighboring indices differ only in derived fields.

Alternative definitions for endianness selection, physical range maximum, granule family and kernel tag exclusion are mutually exclusive per build. Assuming a fixed page size, fixed endianness, fixed large-page support or a fixed exclusion mask across builds misinterprets control words and feature bounds.
